W3 (cost lens), after E003.

What was measured:
- E001: 9 epochs, eager, 0.7430 accuracy in 9.43 s.
- E002: 10 epochs, eager, 0.7495 in 10.55 s.
- E003: torch.compile with max-autotune-no-cudagraphs plus foreach SGD, apparently at 10 epochs (its 0.7486 matches E002), 0.7486 in 12.07 s.

Epoch slope: about +0.65 pp and about +1.1 s per epoch (about 11% of the run). That price still holds.
- 1 pp of accuracy is about 1.5 epochs, about 1.65 s.
- To clear 0.753 from 0.7495 at 10 epochs, eager, takes about 10.6 epochs, about 11.2 s.
- A 40-seed-safe point of about 0.756 needs about 11 epochs, about 11.6 s.

My miss on E003: I priced compile as a pure 12-18% per-epoch saving. The measurement was +1.5 s (+14%). The likely mechanisms are:
- (a) Recompiles or autotuning leaking into timed code. For example, the model sees new guards: train/eval mode flips, an LR change, or parameters reassigned in prepare such as the whitening weight copy or reset.
- (b) Dynamo guard and launch overhead under the 4-CPU pin, which exceeds what fusion saves. The net is small: 48 steps per epoch of about 20 ms, which may already be cuDNN-conv-bound.
- (c) Compiled backward kernels slower than cuDNN for the fp16 channels_last convs.

Accuracy was unchanged (within noise), so the math is fine. Lesson: on this net, systems levers are cheap in accuracy but can backfire on time. Fixed one-off leaks of about 1-2 s are plausible, and only measurement settles them. I now expect compile to save at best about 5-10% once leaks are removed, with real risk of no gain.

Fixed cost in the eager recipe: about 0.3 s or less (uint8 transfer, eigh on 5k images, pad). H3.2 is a small lever. The ragged batch is already dropped (n//bs), so I006's "drop ragged" is a no-op. Its only value is diagnosing E003's leak.

Accounting for levers, in epoch-equivalents (about 1.1 s each):
- EMA/Lookahead: perhaps +0.1-0.3 pp for about 1-3% time, so a net gain of about 0-0.3 epoch. Small and below the single-run noise floor.
- Progressive resizing at 24/28/32 px: about 25% fewer FLOPs per epoch, but likely only 12-18% less wall time (launch overhead, plus interpolate). Its accuracy cost of about 0.5-1 pp needs about 0.8-1.5 epochs to repay, so the net is about zero or negative.
- Muon at batch 2000: half the steps, plus Newton-Schulz overhead. CIFAR-10 hyperparameters ported to CIFAR-100 with no tuning probably lose 0.5-2 pp. Negative unless tuned.

Noise: I assume per-seed std of about 0.2-0.35 pp (3-seed SE about 0.15-0.2 pp) and run-to-run time drift of 1-2%. Single-run differences under 0.3 pp cannot be resolved, so EMA-sized effects need replication.

Best path: raise epochs to about 10.75-11 (the only reliable lever, at about 11.4 s). In parallel, diagnose the compile leak (log recompiles, use mode='default' and reduce-overhead/CUDA graphs, compile only the model and not the optimizer). Then test EMA at the feasible epoch count.

Unsure about:
- whether E003's slowdown is a one-off leak (fixable) or a per-step cost;
- per-seed std;
- whether the slope flattens above 10 epochs.

forecasts.reason: EMA likely adds 0-0.3 pp for 1-3% time. That is below single-run noise, and at 9 epochs it stays well under 0.753.
A byte-identical rerun should drift under 2% in time, with per-seed std around 0.2-0.35 pp.
The ragged batch is already dropped, so this changes nothing unless the agent also finds the real leak. A ≥0.3 s gain is unlikely to come from this change itself.
Untuned Muon at batch 2000 halves the step count on CIFAR-100 and adds Newton-Schulz overhead, so a 10% epoch saving is unlikely.
It saves about 12-18% of wall time but likely loses 0.5-1 pp, far over the 0.2 pp allowance.

cruxes: Is E003's +1.5 s a one-off recompile/autotune leak into prepare/train (fixable, so compile could net -5 to -10%) or a per-step cost under the 4-CPU pin (so compile is a dead end)?
What is the per-seed accuracy std? It sets whether about 10.6 epochs (0.753) or about 11+ epochs (0.756) is the real target, roughly a 0.5 s difference.
Does the accuracy-vs-epoch slope stay near 0.65 pp/epoch above 10 epochs, or flatten, which would make epochs an expensive way to buy margin?
